items.title: Ken Poston interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2024
items.q: And I knew that ideally what Pete Rugolo and Shorty Rogers and Bud Shank and some guys like that, what they wanted really

ctx.x: It depends what it is and what we’re doing because kind of the sequence of events for me was what used to be KLON Radio in Long Beach, which now is K-JAZZ, so I was there for 13 or 14 years producing concerts and festivals and on the air as well. Then the Los Angeles Jazz Institute, which I still operate the Jazz Institute, but then almost ten years ago now I became the general manager at KSDS in San Diego because I truly wanted to see jazz radio continue. And I decided I could continue to do all the other things…

again, you know there’s — our job with radio is to promote what the local promoters are doing, to try to help them, not to compete against them. So we do things — again — for a purpose. Sometimes the purpose is as a fundraiser for the radio station. Sometimes it’s to showcase something or an artist or maybe to celebrate a historical occasion or to celebrate something — a new release, or whatever the case may be. Jazz Institute is a little bit different in that the archive is the centerpiece of the Jazz Institute.…

That’s nice that you’re able to marry those two aspects of your career together. I’ve had a similar thing I’ve been able to do with our archive and a local Arts-In-Education institute over the years, and it really works well if you think it out.
